items.readable_text:
Content:
The product rule for radicals states that the square root of a product equals the product of the square roots:
[MATH: \eqalign{
\sqrt{ab} &=\sqrt{a} \cdot \sqrt{b}
}]

Content:
We can use the product rule to rewrite the square roots of algebraic expressions.

Content:
As an example, let's suppose we want to simplify the following expression:

Content:
[MATH: \sqrt{32y}]

Content:
First, we rewrite [MATH: 32y] as the product [MATH: 16 \cdot 2y,] which contains a perfect square [MATH: (16){:}]

Content:
[MATH: \eqalign{
\sqrt{32y}&=\[5pt]
\sqrt{16 \cdot 2y}&=\[5pt]
\sqrt{4^2 \cdot 2y}&

}]

Content:
Then, we separate the product into two separate radicals using the product rule:

Content:
[MATH: \eqalign{
\sqrt{4^2\cdot 2y}&=\[3pt]
\sqrt{4^2}\cdot \sqrt{2y}&
}]

Content:
Finally, we simplify the radical containing the perfect square:

Content:
[MATH: \eqalign{
\sqrt{4^2}\cdot \sqrt{2y}&=\[3pt]
|4|\cdot \sqrt{2y}&=\[3pt]

4\sqrt{2y}&
}]

sections.normalized_html:
We first write [MATH: 8z^3] as the product [MATH: 4z^2 \cdot 2z] which contains a perfect square [MATH: (4z^2){:}]

[MATH: \eqalign{ \sqrt{8z^3}&=\[3pt] \sqrt{4z^2 \cdot 2z}& }]

Then, we can separate the product into two separate radicals:

[MATH: \eqalign{ \sqrt{4z^2 \cdot 2z}&=\[3pt] \sqrt{(2z)^2\cdot 2z}&=\[3pt] \sqrt{(2z)^2}\cdot \sqrt{2z}& }]

Finally, we simplify the radical containing the perfect square:

[MATH: \eqalign{ \sqrt{(2z)^2}\cdot \sqrt{2z}&=\[3pt] |2z|\cdot \sqrt{2z}&=\[3pt] |2|\cdot|z|\cdot \sqrt{2z}&=\[3pt] 2|z|\sqrt{2z}& }]

sections.normalized_html:
We first write [MATH: 18y^3] as the product [MATH: 9y^2\cdot 2y] which contains a perfect square [MATH: (9y^2).] Then, we separate the product into two separate radicals, one of which can be simplified:

[MATH: \eqalign{ \sqrt{18y^3} &= \ \sqrt{9y^2 \cdot 2y} &= \ \sqrt{9y^2} \cdot \sqrt{2y} &= \ \sqrt{(3y)^2} \cdot \sqrt{2y} &= \ |3y| \cdot \sqrt{2y} &= \ |3| \cdot |y| \cdot \sqrt{2y} &= \ 3 \cdot |y| \cdot \sqrt{2y} }]

Since [MATH: y \geq 0,] we have [MATH: |y|=y,] and we can simplify further. Therefore, our final answer is

[MATH: \eqalign{ 3 \cdot |y| \cdot \sqrt{2y} &= \ 3 \cdot y \cdot \sqrt{2y} &= \ 3y\sqrt{2y}. & }]

[MATH: \eqalign{
\sqrt{18y^3} &= \
\sqrt{9y^2 \cdot 2y} &= \
\sqrt{9y^2} \cdot \sqrt{2y} &= \
\sqrt{(3y)^2} \cdot \sqrt{2y} &= \
|3y| \cdot \sqrt{2y} &= \
|3| \cdot |y| \cdot \sqrt{2y} &= \
3 \cdot |y| \cdot \sqrt{2y}
}]

Since [MATH: y \geq 0,] we have [MATH: |y|=y,] and we can simplify further. Therefore, our final answer is

[MATH: \eqalign{
3 \cdot |y| \cdot \sqrt{2y} &= \
3 \cdot y \cdot \sqrt{2y} &= \
3y\sqrt{2y}. &
}]
